milestones.title: Outside: a real street
milestones.summary: Replace the painted backdrop with a 3D neighbourhood street seen from a third-floor window: a Blender-built street, its own sky and haze, lit on its own layer so parallax sells the space.

items.text: Street pipeline: art/models/street (Blender) to godot/art/street/street.glb
Blockout: our facade, sidewalks, curbs, road with parking lanes, a cross street, the far row of buildings, rooftops behind, a distant skyline
Sky dome per mood (gradient, stars, moon, sun, clouds) and distance haze
In game: street on its own render layer with its own sun/moon and ambient; painted view retired
Shots from several angles, including the fish's view through the tank
Fixes along the way: closed the room's wall corners, sharp-edged boxes in every model (false light in the corner), the stand's z-fighting door panels

milestones.title: Outside: buildings
milestones.summary: Facades that read as a real neighbourhood: brick rowhouses and a corner shop, with rooms behind the windows.

items.text: Facade kit: brick, stucco and clapboard, cornices with brackets and dentils, flat, hooded and arched lintels, stoops, bay windows, fire escapes
Window rooms: interior-mapped rooms behind the glass, lit by mood, with curtains, blinds and sheers, TVs, and cats and plants on the sills; sky reflections
Ground floor shops: awnings, painted signs, neon in the windows, a RAMEN blade sign, shelves and counters inside, a laundromat with washers
Rooftops: water towers, chimneys, bulkheads, AC units, vents, parapets
A faded TORTELLINI'S ghost sign on a bare party wall
Railings, fences and fire-escape gratings as cut-out panels (see-through, and far fewer triangles)
Cars rebuilt: lofted bodies with glass, pillars, wheels in wells, mirrors and lights; taxis

milestones.title: Outside: street life
milestones.summary: The things that fill a street: trees, lamps, parked cars, wires, clutter, and traffic that passes by.

items.text: Street trees with leaf sprays that shade as round crowns; the one by our window low enough to look over
Street lamps, traffic signals that take turns, street signs, hydrants, bins, a mailbox, bike racks, café tables and an A-frame
Parked cars; cars that drive past, stop at red and light the road ahead at night
Telephone poles and wires, with drops across the street to our building
People walking the sidewalks, dressed at random, with umbrellas in the rain (far sidewalk widened to fit them)
A flock of pigeons now and then at golden hour

milestones.title: Outside: moods
milestones.summary: Each mood lights the street its own way.

items.text: Night: lamp pools on the pavement and facades, lit windows and shops, neon, stars, a low moon
Rainy evening: falling rain in sheets at several depths, wet road and puddles that ring with drops and reflect the lights, heavier haze, umbrellas
Golden hour: a warm sky and haze that keep their colour, the low sun behind the far row casting long shadows toward us
Room: sunlit window reveals no longer glow like a lightbox (bright bake eased off above white)
Quality: street sun shadows from Medium, shop, neon and headlight lights from Medium, half the people on Low; about 2 ms a frame on High

milestones.title: Rain on the glass
milestones.summary: Drops that run down, not up, and behave like water.

items.text: Fix: running drops move downward (the pattern scrolled the wrong way for the pane's UVs)
Beads are tiny lenses: each shows the street behind it shrunken and upside down, with a dark rim and a glint
Beads come and go; runners stall and lurch, wander a little, wipe the beads in their way and leave a wet, beaded trail that dries
Fine mist over the glass; drop sizes in real millimetres, fading out below a pixel instead of sparkling
--frames and --frame-step for screenshot sequences

milestones.title: Fish polish
milestones.summary: A friendlier face and a more natural swim.

items.text: Mouth: a blunt, rounded snout with an upper and a fuller lower lip over a dark mouth, instead of the puckered point; the lower lip drops now and then in a gulp
Eyes: crisp gold irises, a darker rim and round pupils as their own caps (painted vertices left them jagged)
Body: a fantail's egg that stays full and pinches into the peduncle rather than a cone; procedural scales
Swimming: the spine bends and cross-sections turn with it (no shearing); the fin flutter weights were upside down (glTF flips v), so the whole body pulsed; fixed
--fish-pose to hold the fish swimming in place for screenshots; frame strips of the swim and a gulp

milestones.title: Polish pass
milestones.summary: Look at everything together, from every angle and mood; performance on each quality level.

items.text: Review pass across moods and cameras: room, fish, room camera, tank cam, street level
Performance: about 2 ms a frame on High and 1.1 ms on Low at 1600x900 (discrete GPU)
Retired the painted views and the backdrop in the room build (lightmap UVs verified unchanged, bakes kept)
Guide updated for the street; tracker shots.json covers the street, the rain and the fish

milestones.title: Look like Tortellini
milestones.summary: Model the fish on the real Tortellini (art/reference/tortellini.jpg): a longer fantail with a red cap, silvery cheeks and belly, small realistic eyes and long, flowing, translucent fins.

items.text: Body: longer and deeper than the cartoon egg, a gently humped back, a slightly bumpy red head cap
Colour: red-orange head, deep orange body, silvery-white cheeks, gill cover and belly patch, a few pale scales
Eyes: small, gold-ringed and realistic
Fins: tall sail dorsal; a long double tail with pointed lobes that droop and flow; long trailing pelvic and anal fins; translucent orange fading paler at the edges
Swimming tuned for the longer fins (they trail and drape more); side-by-side with the photo

milestones.title: Tortellini's shape
milestones.summary: The body outline traced from the photo of Tortellini instead of guessed at.

items.text: Body built from the photo's top and bottom contours: a forehead climbing steeply from the snout, the back peaking before the dorsal, a deep belly, a short thick peduncle
Egg-shaped cross-section, narrower along the back
Eye placed where the photo has it; the red cap reaches further back over the head
Tall sail of a dorsal fin; pelvic fins moved forward under the chest

milestones.title: A moss ball to push around
milestones.summary: The fish can nudge and knock the moss ball around the tank, like a beach ball in water.

items.text: Knocked along the contact normal, harder the faster the fish is going; the fish isn't slowed
No gravity: it drifts, slows in the water and rolls as it goes
Bounces off the glass, gravel, surface and solid decor
The layout keeps where the editor put it; moving it in the editor stills it
--fish-drive for screenshots of the fish swimming on its own

milestones.title: Camera at the top and bottom of the tank
milestones.summary: Near the gravel or the surface the camera keeps its angle and slides in close; the fish fades so it doesn't block the view. The same fade clears the fish out of the way of the monitor when looking at it.

items.text: Against the gravel or the water surface the camera slides in along its line of sight (down to 3 cm) instead of being pushed flat
Up close it looks at the fish itself, not above it, so steep angles hold
The fish fades by a dither (body and fins) when a camera is that close; the room camera and tank cam never see it fade
--look=PITCH to aim the follow camera in screenshots
Looking at the monitor (gaze or the menu) with the fish in front of it: the fish fades the same way

milestones.title: Steering options
milestones.summary: A Steering setting on the monitor: Turn the fish (fish-relative, as before) or Swim where you point (camera-relative).

items.text: Steering: Turn the fish: forward swims the way the fish faces, back backs up, left and right turn
Steering: Swim where you point: the stick is a direction in the view, tilt included (up swims away from the camera, diving when it looks down, climbing when it looks up); the fish arcs round to it
In Swim where you point the camera stays where it's aimed (no swinging round behind the fish)
Saved in settings; controls hint and guide follow it; --steering for a single run

milestones.title: Split-screen co-op
milestones.summary: More fish in the same tank, each piloted by a local player, on a split screen. Every fish presses the same cards, which drive the one virtual controller on the host.

items.text: Decided: all fish share the one virtual controller on the host, and live in the same tank
Decided: up to 4 fish; two side by side, three or four in quarters
Decided: pressing a button on an unused gamepad drops a new fish in; player 1 may use keyboard and mouse or a pad, everyone else a pad
Decided: each player picks their fish's colouring in their own view on joining; everyone's are on the monitor's Players page
Decided: opening the menu takes everyone to the monitor menu, full screen; any pad drives it
Decided: sound heard from the middle of the fish
Fish colourings to pick from, named for pasta: Linguini, Fusilli (calico), Gnocchi (red cap on white), Ravioli (black and orange)
Players: each with its own fish, input device, follow camera, steering and look
Split-screen views, and the join flow with its colouring chooser
Shared cards: any fish in front of a card presses it (holds combine, toggles flip on any arrival, a sequence plays once while it's already playing)
Fish bump each other and the moss ball; the tank cam tracks every fish
Leaving: from the monitor, or by holding Back
Quality: each extra view costs about 0.4 ms (four players on High: 3.2 ms a frame on an RTX 3080); views follow the quality level's anti-aliasing and scale
Controls page on the monitor: a column per player, each worked at once by its own player's pad (player 1's keyboard and mouse in theirs), with a turning fish carousel
Per player: steering, invert look and look speed (player 1's are remembered)
Monitor tidied: the home page keeps the hosts and Just swim / Edit tank / Controls / Settings / Quit; graphics, mood, tank cam and volumes are on a Settings page; button art is in the tank editor
Settings page in sections (Display, Tank cam, Sound) of label ◀ value ▶ rows, the same Stepper as the Controls page's; Back at the bottom; no controls listing on the main menu

milestones.title: Low-end check
milestones.summary: Run on integrated graphics, which Auto puts on Low, and tune what Low keeps. On an Intel N150 at 1080p, Low now holds 60 fps in the menu and swimming, with a stream on the monitor; the tank editor and split screen hold 30.

items.text: --bench and tools/bench.sh: a fixed tour of views (menu, swimming, tank editor, split screen, room, window) in every mood and quality level, with and without a 1080p60 stream, timing frame and GPU ms; a headless Sway reaches the real GPU without a desktop
Measured on an Intel N150 (1080p): Low was 33-41 ms a frame in the menu and swimming, 45-64 ms in the editor, 43-54 ms split; Medium 49-117 ms and High 75-155 ms, left as they are
Low: the room drawn from its bake alone (unshaded); no live lamps, fairy lights, LED strip or screen glow; the window's light only at golden hour; no tank lamp shadow
Low: unshaded tank glass; rain on the window drawn over the view instead of bending it (no copy of the screen each frame)
Low street: lamps stop short of the room, no light through the tree leaves; people and cars keep moving
Stream uploads in 512 px regions instead of 64 (a 1080p60 stream cost up to 3 ms a frame, now about 0.5-1.5); algae on the tank glass skips its noise where there is none
Low now: menu 12-15 ms, swimming 15.6-16.3 ms (16.9 at golden hour with a stream), room 13-16 ms, editor 25-32 ms and split 24-26 ms (target 30 fps there), street from the window 15-19.5 ms
Tank cuts (water surface, bubbles, motes, plant sway) measured at under 0.5 ms together on this GPU, so left as they are
